daily_reality.summary: Internal medicine physicians (internists) provide comprehensive adult care in primary care and hospital settings. They spend significant time on EHR documentation (~7.3 hours per 8 hours of patient time), patient encounters, rounds, and care coordination. Burnout from documentation burden is a major concern.
typical_tasks: Conduct patient encounters (history, physical exam, assessment, plan)
Document in EHR systems (chart review, notes, orders — ~16 min per encounter)
Order and interpret diagnostic tests (labs, imaging)
Prescribe medications and manage chronic disease regimens
Coordinate care with specialists and allied health professionals
Conduct preventive health screenings and wellness visits
Review and respond to patient messages and test results
Participate in care conferences, tumor boards, and quality meetings
Complete after-hours documentation ('pajama time' — avg 1.4 hrs/day outside clinic)
key_documents: Quality measures and MIPS reporting documentation

deadlines.documentation: Within 24-48 hours of patient encounter (best practice)
deadlines.lab_result_review: Same day or next business day
deadlines.mips_reporting: Annual reporting by March 31 for prior year

daily_reality.seasonality: Flu season (Oct-March) increases patient volume. January brings new insurance/deductible resets driving appointment surges. Holiday periods create coverage challenges. Medicare annual wellness visits cluster in Q4.

regulatory.summary: Requires MD/DO degree, 3-year residency, state medical license, and ABIM board certification. Maintenance of Certification (MOC) requires 100 points every 5 years and assessment every 10 years. 260,000+ ABIM-certified physicians in the US.

key_laws.name: State Medical Practice Acts
key_laws.description: Each state's medical board governs physician licensing, renewal, and discipline

key_laws.name: MACRA / MIPS
key_laws.description: Medicare payment reform tying reimbursement to quality measures, cost, interoperability, and improvement activities

key_laws.name: HIPAA
key_laws.description: Patient privacy and health information security requirements

key_laws.name: Stark Law / Anti-Kickback Statute
key_laws.description: Physician self-referral and financial relationship regulations

requirements: MD or DO degree from accredited medical school (4 years)
State medical license (renewal every 1-3 years by state)
ABIM Board Certification in Internal Medicine
DEA registration for prescribing controlled substances
licensing.moc_requirements: 100 MOC points every 5 years; assessment every 10 years (traditional exam or LKA — Longitudinal Knowledge Assessment preferred 4:1)
licensing.cme: 50+ CME hours annually (varies by state); up to 164 credits available at ACP Annual Meeting 2026

regulatory.penalties: State medical board discipline (probation, suspension, revocation). CMS penalties for MIPS non-compliance. Malpractice liability. DEA enforcement for controlled substance violations.

tools.summary: EHR systems (Epic leads with 38% hospital market share) dominate daily workflow. AI documentation assistants are emerging rapidly. Diagnostic equipment and clinical decision support tools supplement clinical work.

primary_tools.name: Epic EHR
primary_tools.description: Leading hospital EHR system (3,600+ US hospitals, 38% market share). Embedding generative AI for documentation assistance.

primary_tools.name: Oracle Health (formerly Cerner)
primary_tools.description: Major EHR system with Clinical AI Agent reducing documentation time by ~30%

primary_tools.name: NextGen Healthcare
primary_tools.description: Ranked #1 EHR vendor in internal medicine for ambulatory practices

primary_tools.name: UpToDate
primary_tools.description: Evidence-based clinical decision support — most widely used point-of-care resource

primary_tools.name: Epocrates / DynaMed
primary_tools.description: Drug reference and clinical information at point of care

secondary_tools: Stethoscope, otoscope, ophthalmoscope — physical exam basics
AI scribes (Nuance DAX, Freed AI, Abridge) — ambient documentation
Athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, Practice Fusion — ambulatory EHRs
pain_points: EHR documentation burden (7.3 hours per 8 hours of patient time)
Prior authorization requirements consuming physician time
Interoperability issues between different EHR systems
Alert fatigue from excessive clinical decision support notifications
After-hours documentation ('pajama time') affecting work-life balance

terminology.summary: Internal medicine uses extensive medical terminology, documentation abbreviations, and clinical assessment frameworks. SOAP notes and H&P format are fundamental documentation structures.

terms.H&P: History and Physical — formal comprehensive patient assessment document
terms.SOAP: Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan — standard note format
terms.ROS: Review of Systems — checklist assessment of symptoms by organ system
terms.HPI: History of Present Illness — detailed current complaint narrative
terms.CC: Chief Complaint — main reason for the visit
terms.HEENT: Head, Eyes, Ears, Nose, Throat — physical exam section
terms.PRN: Pro Re Nata — as needed (medication dosing)
terms.NPO: Nil Per Os — nothing by mouth

career_psychology.summary: High-demand, high-stress specialty with average salary ~$345K. Burnout exceeds 50% driven by documentation burden and administrative tasks. The field faces a projected shortfall of 14,900-35,600 physicians. Meaningful patient relationships provide core satisfaction.
career_path: Medical school — MD or DO (4 years)
General Internist / Hospitalist (or fellowship for subspecialty)
fears: Loss of clinical autonomy to administrative mandates
Prior authorization denials affecting patient care
motivation: Intellectual challenge of complex diagnostic medicine
Making a difference in patient health outcomes
Respected profession with high social value
burnout_factors: EHR documentation burden (~11.4 hour effective workdays)
Patient volume pressure reducing per-patient time
Burnout costs US healthcare $4.6 billion/year in turnover

community.summary: Large, established professional community led by ACP (163,000 members) and SGIM (3,300+ academic internists). Rich conference ecosystem, subspecialty organizations, and online communities.

associations.name: American College of Physicians (ACP)
associations.description: 163,000 members worldwide — largest medical specialty society, advocacy, CME, clinical guidance

associations.name: Society of General Internal Medicine (SGIM)
associations.description: 3,300+ academic general internists, 70+ Interest Groups on GIM Connect platform

associations.name: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM)
associations.description: Board certification for 260,000+ internists across 20 disciplines

associations.name: Association of Chiefs and Leaders of GIM (ACLGIM)
associations.description: SGIM sub-group for leadership development in academic GIM

online_communities: GIM Connect — SGIM member-only online platform (70+ Interest Groups)
Doximity — physician networking and telehealth platform
conferences: ACP Internal Medicine Meeting 2026 (San Francisco, April 16-18)
ACP Internal Medicine Board Review Course

market.summary: Critical physician shortage with projected 14,900-35,600 internist deficit. Internal medicine is most in-demand specialty for locum tenens. Average salary ~$345K-$391K with strong geographic variation. 3% employment growth projected 2024-2034.
market.growth_rate: 3% projected 2024-2034 (23,600 annual openings across all physicians)
market.physician_shortage: 14,900 - 35,600 projected primary care physician shortfall; up to 86,000 total physician shortage by 2036 (AAMC)
top_employers: Large physician groups and health networks
market_trends: Most in-demand locum tenens specialty in 2024
2026 Medicare conversion factor increase to ~$33.57 (first real increase in years)
AI documentation assistants reducing EHR burden
Shift from private practice to employed physician models
Telehealth integration expanding access and practice flexibility
Value-based care models changing reimbursement structure
